explain.say: Imagine a drum that can talk: it can ring like a bell, boom like thunder and even slide up and down like a voice. That is the tabla, from North India. Here is the secret: the tabla is two drums. Look at the board: the dayan on the right and the bayan on the left.

explain.say: Look at the dayan, the smaller drum, carved from wood and played with the right hand. See the black circle on top? It is called the syahi, a paste of iron filings and flour, and it makes the drum ring with a clear note. Why do you think a drum needs a note?

explain.say: Now look at the bayan, the bigger drum, made of metal or clay, played with the left hand. It makes deep booms, and when the player presses and slides the heel of the palm, the boom bends up and down like a voice. Can you make a boom sound with your voice that slides up?

explain.say: Tabla players speak their rhythms as syllables called bols, like Dha, Dhin and Ta. Look at the circle: teentaal, a cycle of 16 beats in four groups of four. The first beat is sam, the strongest one, where everyone lands together. Can you say Dha Dhin Dhin Dha?

stages.label: Dha Dhin Dhin Dha
stages.note: Beats 5 to 8: the same pattern again

stages.note: Beats 9 to 12: khali, the open, empty part

stages.label: Ta Dhin Dhin Dha
stages.note: Beats 13 to 16: the bass returns, back to sam

explain.say: Brilliant! Look at the third group: Dha Tin Tin Ta. This is khali, which means empty, because the bass drum goes quiet, so listeners know where they are in the cycle. Wow fact: the late Zakir Hussain played tabla on stages all over the world. Challenge: clap the 16 beats and say the bols!

faq.a: The dayan is the smaller, higher drum of the tabla, carved from wood and played with the right hand by most players. It is tuned to a set note.
asks: What is the right-hand tabla drum?
Is the dayan made of wood?

faq.a: The bayan is the larger bass drum of the tabla, usually made of metal or clay and played with the left hand. Pressing with the palm bends its pitch.
asks: What is the left-hand tabla drum?
Why does the tabla bass bend?

faq.q: Why does the tabla have a black circle?
faq.a: The black circle is the syahi, a layered paste of iron filings, flour and gum. Its weight helps the drum ring with clear, musical notes instead of a dull thud.
asks: What is the black spot on a tabla?

faq.a: Sam is the first and most important beat of a rhythm cycle. Musicians often finish phrases exactly on sam, and listeners may nod or clap there.
asks: What is the first beat of a taal?
What does sam mean in Indian music?

faq.a: Khali means empty. It is the part of the cycle where the bass drum is left out, so players and listeners can tell where they are. In teentaal it is beat 9.
asks: What is the wave in teentaal?

facts: Teentaal, the most common rhythm cycle in Hindustani music, has 16 beats in four groups of four.
The black circle on a tabla head, the syahi, contains iron filings.
Zakir Hussain (1951–2024) was one of the world's best-known tabla players.

quiz.say: How many beats are in teentaal?
quiz.why: Teentaal has 16 beats, in four groups of four.

wrong.1: Four is the size of each group, not the whole cycle.
wrong.2: Seven-beat cycles exist, like rupak, but teentaal has 16.

quiz.say: Which tabla drum makes the deep, booming sounds?
quiz.show: The deep booms come from the…
quiz.why: The bayan is the larger bass drum played with the left hand.

wrong.1: The dayan is the smaller drum with higher, ringing notes.
wrong.2: The syahi is the black patch on the drumhead, not a drum.
